record.original_question: Keep the opaque-square barrier condition that every line meeting the boundary of the square must also meet the barrier C, and add the requirement that two inhabitants located at opposite vertices of the square must be able to go from one house to the other through the square without climbing over the barrier. Under this added passage constraint, does there exist a barrier C of minimal total length, and what is it?

evidence.quote: Une variante du problème posé est comme suit : finalement, deux habitants dans deux sommets opposés (seulement deux sur les quatre) souhaitent aller l’un chez l’autre en passant par le square, sans avoir à escalader la palissade. Question : peut-on toujours trouver une palissade C de longueur minimale respectant la contrainte énoncée plus haut et la nouvelle introduite ici ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S = [0,1]^2$ be the closed unit square in the plane. A barrier (opaque set) for $S$ is a closed set $C \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that every straight line in the plane which meets the boundary $\partial S$ also meets $C$. Equivalently, $C$ blocks every line of sight crossing $S$. The length of $C$ is its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(C)$.

Impose the following additional passage constraint: fix two opposite vertices $A$ and $B$ of $S$ (say $A=(0,0)$ and $B=(1,1)$). Require that there exists a continuous path $\gamma : [0,1] \to S$ with $\gamma(0)=A$, $\gamma(1)=B$, and $\gamma((0,1)) \cap C = \emptyset$ (so a traveller can walk inside the square from $A$ to $B$ without crossing the barrier).

Question: Among all closed sets $C \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying both the opaque-set condition and the passage constraint above, does there exist one of minimum total length $\mathcal{H}^1(C)$? If so, describe such a minimizer explicitly and give its length.
artifact.status_search_result: The classical opaque square problem (without passage constraint) is itself open: no exact minimum is known, the best known construction has length about 2.639, and even existence of a minimizer in the general class is not fully settled. The variant with an added passage constraint between two opposite vertices is a strengthening of this open problem and does not appear to have been resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Opaque set - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: No exact algorithm is currently known even for the simplest instances such as a square or an equilateral triangle... conjectured to be the best possible more generally, but this remains unproven.
status_evidence.claim: The opaque square problem remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Opaque Square (Dumitrescu)
status_evidence.snippet: Best known construction for the opaque square has length approximately 2.639; optimality is open.
status_evidence.claim: Even the basic opaque square minimum is unknown, so the passage variant is at least as open.
